_why: PUBLIC CONFIGURATION, DELIBERATELY COMMITTED. Every value here is a fact anyone can read off
the open internet or off a deploy script already in this repo. None of it is a secret, and
treating it as one is what stalled the release controller.
THE DEFECT THIS CLOSES. `doctor` held BOTH environments on four values --
BUILDANDDO_{STAGING,PRODUCTION}_{URL,DEPLOY_MODE} -- which it would only read from a secrets
file at D:\citadel_secrets\BuildAndDo\release.env that has never existed. Meanwhile
scripts/deploy/ship.py has been deploying both environments for weeks with the same URLs
hardcoded at lines 73-74. The controller was blocked on knowing its own public hostname while
the shipping tool beside it had that hostname as a literal.
So the blocker was never a missing credential. It was public config filed under secrets, and a
second source of truth for a fact the repo already stated.
WHAT STILL BELONGS IN THE SECRETS FILE: BUILDANDDO_{env}_HOST, _USER and _SSH_KEY_FILE. Those
are real credentials and they are NOT here. With this file in place `doctor` still HOLDs both
environments -- but it now names those three as missing instead of the URL, which is the
accurate statement of what is actually absent. Naming the wrong gap is worse than naming none:
it sent people to write a URL into a vault instead of placing a key.

_provenance.deploy_mode: ship.py rsyncs a built dist to a remote VM over SSH, which is ssh_webroot
